stem:
The diagram shows trapezium $ABCD$ with $AB\parallel DC$ and equal non-parallel sides $AD=BC$. Diya studies whether the base angles are equal.

Which two claims are correct?

options.text: The trapezium has equal base angles because it is labelled $ABCD$.
The non-parallel sides are equal because the base angles are already equal.

teacher.key_rationale: Equal non-parallel sides make an isosceles trapezium, so base angles at A and B are equal and base angles at D and C are equal. Labelling ABCD alone does not force equal angles. Treating equal base angles as the cause of equal legs reverses the relation.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source triangle into isosceles trapezium ABCD with equal non-parallel sides marked.
